# FishHist: Southeast Fisheries Management History Data Package <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="138" style="padding: 10px"/></a>

<!-- badges: start -->

<!-- badges: end -->

## Overview 

Fisheries management history data are essential for properly understanding trends in fishery-dependent data as well as results from stock assessment models. Federal regulations are published under Federal Registrar (FR) notices. In the Southeast US region under the Southeast Data Assessment and Review (SEDAR) process, management histories for an upcoming stock assessment were previously provided on a species by species basis, and often lacked consistent documentation to the FR notice where the rule was published. To standardize the collection of these data, a Southeast Fisheries Management History Database was build and populated for Federal Management Plans (FMPs) throughout the Gulf of America, South Atlantic, and U.S. Caribbean regions. Compilation of this database was a collaborative process involving South Atlantic Fishery Management Council (SAFMC), Gulf Fishery Management Council (GFMC), Southeast Regional Office (SERO), and Southeast Fisheries Science Center (SEFSC) personnel. Funding for this project beginning in 2020 was made possible through NOAA's Fisheries Information System (FIS) program. In total, this project entered FRs from 16 FMPs within the Southeast region.

Each record within the database contains a regulation from a FR notice, however in this raw format, the individual management actions are disjointed because each rule often overwrites or changes an existing rule. The FishHist data set within this package contains an analysis-ready Fisheries Management History data set that links and reconciles overlapping actions that modify or replace prior rules over time. Functions built within this package assist in visualizing and analyzing fisheries management history data for science and management.

## Publications
